title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: What do the adoption figures actually describe `[V]`?
options: A forecast of where AI responsibility will sit within three years

The present — in roughly half of organizations surveyed, internal comms is already heavily involved in or solely responsible for AI rollout communication, with 40% also on strategy and adoption workstreams
What practitioners believe their role ought to be
The share of organizations that have completed an AI rollout
questions.explanation: n=448 North American IC professionals, fielded December 2025. Reading it as a forecast misses the point: the work is arriving now, and the question is whether you claim it deliberately or receive it by default.

questions.prompt: Why does the ~16% figure make the opportunity larger rather than smaller?
options: Because it shows HR lacks the capability to lead AI change
Because a responsibility that is arriving anyway, and that its obvious owner has declined, gets assigned rather than competed for
Because it demonstrates that AI adoption is not a People function issue
Because low support means low expectations and easier success
questions.explanation: And it gets assigned to whoever holds the most credible account of how it should work when somebody senior finally asks, which is what the four artifacts from this track are for.

questions.prompt: What is the first cost of claiming the mandate?
options: The additional headcount required to deliver it
Becoming the messenger for the thing people fear most — drawing down a credibility stock you spend faster than you build
The loss of independence from the IT function
Increased scrutiny of the communications budget
questions.explanation: Module 3 established the asymmetry between spending and building credibility. A mandate requiring you to announce unpopular things repeatedly draws down the exact asset the rest of the track exists to protect.

questions.prompt: Why does "AI will augment, not replace" become a liability?
options: Because it is usually false
Because employees do not have access to your reasoning — they have access to the sequence of events, and a vague reassurance later falsified costs more than an honest uncertainty
Because it invites comparison with competitors' messaging
Because it cannot be translated consistently across languages
questions.explanation: If you can't make the commitment specific (which roles, over what period, reviewed when) describing what is genuinely uncertain is the stronger move.

questions.prompt: What happens when an announcement contradicts a reader's direct experience?
options: They assume their own experience is unrepresentative
They discount that specific claim while trusting the rest of the message
They conclude the announcement isn't describing reality — and that judgement transfers to the next announcement, which may be one that matters
They seek clarification through their manager
questions.explanation: Which is why the productivity narrative is dangerous: it lands in front of people whose actual experience includes supervision work nobody counted.

questions.prompt: Why is announcing an AI policy your function doesn't follow described as self-inflicted?
options: Because policies should be written by legal rather than communications
Because your function is the most-observed user of AI in the organization — your output is what everybody sees, so a gap between the policy and your newsletter is published evidence against yourself
Because policy announcements attract more scrutiny than other messages
Because employees rarely read policies but always notice inconsistency
questions.explanation: Which makes Modules 5 and 6 the protection: a trust line you actually hold and a review discipline you actually run are the difference between announcing a standard and demonstrating one.

questions.prompt: What separates a proposal from a request for more capacity?
options: Naming a specific executive sponsor
Including a competitive benchmark
The funding line — what you will stop doing, which is why the kill list asked for three things and their sponsors rather than a principle
Quantifying the return on investment
questions.explanation: A proposal that adds scope without subtracting anything is a request for more capacity dressed as a strategy, and an experienced reader can tell in about four seconds.

questions.prompt: What is the sharpest argument *against* claiming this mandate?
options: That communications lacks the technical knowledge for AI governance
That the function claiming AI adoption in a year of cuts has volunteered to be the face of the cuts — and the people declining to lead may have correctly assessed what comes with it
That IT or Legal will claim it regardless
That the mandate cannot be delivered without additional headcount
questions.explanation: It reframes the 16% as an accurate read rather than timidity, and it is the version most likely to change whether you actually send the proposal, which is why the activity asks you to engage it.
